title: Big bang state versus jet horizon: same vanishing $A_0$, different role; existence is dynamical
html:
Remark. Big bang state versus jet horizon: same vanishing A_0, different role; existence is dynamical

Relation to the jet horizon. A big bang state is algebraically identical to the data on one side of a jet horizon . Both are characterised by the vanishing of A_0. The difference is purely contextual:

Concept Algebraic condition Role
Jet horizon A_0\vert_{\mathcal{H}} = 0 Boundary within an affine chart
Big bang state A_0\vert_{\mathcal{S}_0} = 0 Reference configuration of an affine chart

A jet horizon is a boundary. A big bang state is an initial condition. The same vanishing ideal \mathfrak{h} describes both.

Existence is not assumed. Whether any affine chart in the descended universe admits a big bang state is a dynamical question, not an axiom. The framework accommodates three consistent scenarios:

  • Every affine chart has a big bang state (global initial singularity).
  • Only some charts have a big bang state.
  • No chart has a big bang state (the backward light cone extends indefinitely).
